subject: FinTechCo - multi-region performance & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: FinTechCo discovery recap + suggested next tests

Alicia — great to meet today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Call notes (high level):
- Primary use: low-latency fraud scoring and realtime enrichment across NA & EU customers.
- Traffic profile: ~200 req/s peak per region; 1-2s SLA target for P99 inference.
- Data residency: EU transactional data must remain in eu-west region.
- Current stack: in-house API + GCP/Vertex for some ML endpoints; evaluating Redwood for predictable latency and cost.

Competitive items you asked about:
- Hyperscalers (Vertex/Vertex AI/Vertices endpoints): broadly available but harder to guarantee cross-region latency consistently at our scale without reserved capacity.
- Other inference APIs: simpler to get started but often lack region controls and SLA-backed throughput.

Proposed next steps:
1) We run a Redwood-managed multi-region latency sweep (us-east1, us-west2, eu-west1) using a phenotypic traffic profile you shared; deliver CSV + short report.
2) You run the same traffic profile against your current Vertex endpoints and share raw results (we can help with the runner).
3) Joint compare: P50/P95/P99 latency, cold-start behavior, and cost estimates for production throughput.

I attached a quick benchmark request template to capture the exact traffic shape — if you can fill and return we'll prioritize tests.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: fintechco-benchmark-request.xlsx

From: Alicia Torres <alicia@fintechco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: FinTechCo discovery recap + suggested next tests

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the summary. One clarification before we run anything:
- For EU traffic we need the inference to run in eu-west with no egress of transaction payloads. Is Redwood able to pin requests to EU-only hosts for those keys?

We'll fill the benchmark template and return by EOD tomorrow. I’ll also attach the Vertex results we have from last month — would be helpful if you can annotate where Redwood would differ operationally (reserved capacity, SLA, fallback behaviors).

Alicia
Head of Platform Engineering, FinTechCo

--- Forwarded attachment: vertex-lastmonth-results.zip (not included)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo discovery recap + suggested next tests

Alicia — short answers: yes.
- Redwood Private/Dedicated allows pinning inference for specific API keys to eu-west nodes only (no cross-region egress). We can also provide a Private deployment option if you need an isolated control plane.

Initial competitive note (quick comparison):
- Vertex: strong for model training and first-party integrations; regional availability is broad, but to get predictable P99 you often need reserved capacity + additional orchestration.
- Managed inference APIs: convenient but typically single-region endpoints; few provide SLA-backed multi-region routing or built-in KV/prefix caching we use to improve unit cost.

We’ll schedule the Redwood sweep once we get your filled template. Marissa — can you confirm the test runner parameters and ETA for internal results?

Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Alicia Torres <alicia@fintechco@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood test plan + what we'll measure

Alicia — looping in a short test plan so expectations are clear. We'll run the Redwood runner from three origins (us-east1, us-west2, eu-west1) hitting identical model versions and request patterns you provided.

What we'll measure:
- P50/P95/P99 latencies (in ms) per region
- Cold-start per-node (first request after idle)
- Throughput under sustained 200 req/s (per-region) and 500 req/s burst
- Request tagging to ensure any eu-scoped keys are pinned to eu-west only
- Token-level cost estimate based on your prompt sizes

Deliverables:
- raw-latency-results.csv (CSV with timestamps + latencies)
- redwood-multi-region-latency-report-20260728.pdf (summary with charts and recommendations)
- short mutual action plan: recommended config (Dedicated pools + autoscale config) + next tests for end-to-end integration.

We expect to have the Redwood results back to you by Tue 2026-07-28 EOD. If you prefer an earlier checkpoint, we can share a preliminary CSV within 48 hours.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-test-plan.md (inline)

- P99: 780 ms

Alicia

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood multi-region results + recommended next steps

Alicia / Raj — attaching our completed sweep and a short report. Quick highlights:

Summary (Redwood runner results, identical traffic shape):
- us-east1: P50 35 ms, P95 95 ms, P99 210 ms
- us-west2: P50 40 ms, P95 110 ms, P99 240 ms
- eu-west1 (pinned): P50 50 ms, P95 140 ms, P99 320 ms
- Cold-starts: ~600-800 ms depending on quantization and batch window
- Under sustained 200 req/s per region we sustained P99 under 350 ms with Dedicated pools + autoscale configured.

Key differentiators vs Vertex baseline you sent:
- Lower P99 in eu-west for steady-state when configured with Dedicated pools; Vertex baseline showed a higher tail at spikes (your P99 780ms vs our 320ms).
- Regional pinning: Redwood can pin keys to eu-west and prevent egress; available as a Dedicated/Private option.
- Cost: estimated ~15-25% lower per-token at your throughput when using batching + KV prefix caching; we included cost model in the PDF.

Attachments: redwood-multi-region-latency-report-20260728.pdf; raw-latency-results.csv.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Align on Dedicated pool sizing for a pilot (we recommend 2x T4-equivalent nodes per region to start).
2) Security checklist: we'll provide the EU data residency documentation and SOC 2 evidence for your security team.
3) Schedule a 30-min tech sync (this week) to validate integration config and decide on pilot timelines.

If that sounds right I'll push a short mutual action plan + statement of work draft. Happy to do a quick call to walk through the report.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-multi-region-latency-report-20260728.pdf, raw-latency-results.csv
